core_obligations: Local objects and vanishing (proof lines 1694-1700): a covering is chosen over which the gerbe has local objects, and after refining the covering the first cohomology of the automorphism sheaf on the members and on the pairwise intersections vanishes.

Compare the local objects (proof lines 1701-1733): the isomorphisms between the restrictions of two local objects form a torsor under the automorphism sheaf, hence is trivial by the vanishing, so isomorphisms can be chosen; their deviation from satisfying the cocycle condition is measured by automorphisms of one local object over triple intersections, which are sections of the automorphism sheaf.

Make the comparisons into a descent datum (proof lines 1734-1748): the author notes that a computation shows these sections form a two-cocycle of the automorphism sheaf, the spectral sequence and the vanishing of first cohomology make the comparison map from Cech cohomology in degree two to cohomology injective, so the cocycle is a coboundary; correcting the chosen isomorphisms by the resulting cochain makes them satisfy the cocycle condition, which is a descent datum for the local objects, and the proof is complete.
proof_roadmap: Choose a covering with local objects and refine it so that the first cohomology of the automorphism sheaf vanishes on the pieces and on their intersections.
Use the vanishing to choose isomorphisms between the local objects, and measure their failure to be a cocycle by sections over triple intersections.
Show that failure is a two-cocycle, use the Cech spectral sequence to write it as a coboundary, and correct the isomorphisms to obtain a descent datum.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that an abelian gerbe over a site has an object over an object of the site on which a cofinal system of coverings trivializes the relevant first cohomology and the second cohomology vanishes (statement lines 1676-1691). The proof is a complete descent argument: a covering with local objects is chosen and refined so that first cohomology vanishes on the pieces and their intersections (proof lines 1694-1700); the isom sheaves between local objects are identified as torsors and hence trivialized (proof lines 1701-1733); and the resulting failure of the cocycle condition is measured by a two-cocycle of the automorphism sheaf, which the Cech spectral sequence together with the vanishing shows to be a coboundary, after which the isomorphisms are corrected to give a descent datum (proof lines 1734-1748). The non-formal content is the passage from a trivialized comparison to a descent datum through the cohomological obstruction. The claim is H2: a structured descent argument with every input named.
